question: A district health officer wants to evaluate the DMHP using an *outcome* indicator rather than a process indicator. Which of the following best qualifies as an outcome indicator?

answers.text: Proportion of patients with schizophrenia showing ≥50% reduction in symptom severity at 6 months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is an outcome indicator — it measures change in patient health status attributable to the programme, not just the volume of activities delivered.

answers.text: Number of training sessions conducted for ASHA workers on mental health recognition

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is a process indicator — it records programme activities (training inputs), not the resulting improvement in patient or community health.

answers.text: Percentage of PHCs that have a designated mental health nodal officer

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is a structural/input indicator reflecting programme infrastructure, not patient-level outcomes.

answers.text: Total number of new cases registered at the district mental health facility per quarter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Case registration counts are an output/activity indicator. They reflect service utilisation but not the health impact achieved.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the monitoring section. Outcome indicators measure change in health status; process indicators measure programme activities. Apply that distinction to each option.
Good analysis. Distinguishing process, output, and outcome indicators is critical for meaningful NMHP/DMHP programme evaluation.
